text:
Sarah: quick follow-up from the RFC — should tenant private endpoints be direct (private endpoint in customer VPC) or delegated to a tenant-proxy relay by default? thinking about operational cost, traceability, and cert distribution.

Matt: quick list of constraints i care about: latency SLOs, IP preservation for egress, cert lifecycle complexity, and customer firewall simplicity.

Oliver: +1 on latency. direct endpoints avoid an extra hop but blow up our endpoint count and cross-account peering surface.

Devon: tenant-proxy makes rollout and telemetry easier (single egress point) and lets us do per-tenant caching/batching. downside is extra maintenance and an obvious single point to scale.

Kate: also think about incidents: with direct endpoints, a customer VPC misconfig can take them fully offline. With a proxy we can failover to hosted fallback model more easily.

Matt: cost math quick sketch: direct endpoints => N endpoints ≈ #customers * endpoints-per-customer. proxy => shared fleet with autoscale. tradeoffs: $$ for infra vs ops headcount.

Sarah: also certs: direct requires per-customer cert provision for SNI or mutual TLS. proxy can terminate and reuse our certs but then we need attestation between proxy and control plane.

Oliver: what about routing semantics? If we use proxy, we can keep source IPs via X-Forwarded-For but some customers need true source IP preservation for egress ACLs.

Devon: we sketched a compromise in the RFC: prefer direct for low-traffic, proxy for high-churn or restricted customers. but we left the boundary vague. needs concrete thresholds.

Sarah: propose concrete threshold options to choose from:
- option A: direct by default; proxy opt-in for >X req/s or explicit security request.
- option B: proxy by default; direct opt-in for trusted customers with static IP pools.
- option C: hybrid routing: initial affinity to direct, fallback to proxy on error/latency.

Kate: preference: option C. keeps best-effort latency while giving us a predictable fallback path for incidents.

Matt: can we pick threshold numbers? suggest: if >200 rps sustained or >10k tokens/minute, recommend proxy. numbers are fuzzy, open to engineering input.

Oliver: capacity-wise proxy fleet needs autoscale headroom for bursts; we should define a circuit-breaker policy: e.g., if proxy <-> backend latency > 150ms for 30s then flip to direct (if available).

Devon: sample routing config snippet (proto):
```yaml
routing:
  policy: prefer_direct_with_fallback
  direct_threshold_rps: 200
  fallback_latency_ms: 150
  fallback_window_s: 30
```

Sarah: operational implications:
- telemetry: tag requests with path=direct|proxy, include proxy instance id for tracing.
- security: proxy needs mTLS to control plane and to customer VPC (if we terminate there), or we keep mTLS end-to-end and let proxy be a TCP passthrough.
- onboarding: prefer direct when customer wants minimal peering config changes.

Matt: some customers require IP preservation for downstream partner integrations; for them direct is the only acceptable option. add explicit opt-in in the onboarding playbook.

Kate: action items: Sarah to draft decision appendix with chosen option and thresholds; Devon + Oliver to run capacity/latency sim for proxy fleet; Matt to update onboarding checklist for IP-preservation opt-in.

Sarah: +1 and will tag the RFC follow-up. pinging @infra-bot to start a ticket. :paperclip:

infra-bot: Created ticket INF-3241: "Decision: tenant endpoint delegation vs direct connect — follow-up actions" assigned to Sarah, Devon, Oliver, Matt.

Oliver: tiny note — we should document cert patterns: a) mTLS end-to-end with proxy as passthrough, b) TLS terminate at proxy w/ attestation. both have tradeoffs for inspection and DLP.

Devon: i'll prototype fallback logic and a small sim script this week. will post perf numbers in the thread.

Sarah: thanks — let's reconvene Fri to pick final option. :thumbsup:
